form.title: Cambridge A Level Humanities onboarding test

writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: Which best describes a "short-term cause"?
items.answer: A factor that develops just before an event and brings it closer
options: A factor that develops just before an event and brings it closer
items.markingKey: B. A factor that develops just before an event and brings it closer. Close in time

items.stem: A turning point in history is
items.answer: an event after which things change significantly
options: an event after which things change significantly
items.markingKey: B. an event after which things change significantly. Marks a shift

items.stem: Which is an example of continuity?
items.answer: Most people continued to work on the land after a new king took power
options: Most people continued to work on the land after a new king took power
items.markingKey: A. Most people continued to work on the land after a new king took power. Things staying the same

items.stem: A source that agrees with other independent evidence is said to be
items.answer: corroborated
items.markingKey: C. corroborated. Cross-checked

items.stem: Why might a court chronicle praising a king be unreliable?
items.answer: It was written to please the ruler
options: It was written to please the ruler
It is too old to read
items.markingKey: B. It was written to please the ruler. Patronage

items.stem: A source is biased. Can it still be useful to a historian?
items.answer: Yes, it reveals the attitudes and purposes of its author
options: Only if it is a photograph
Yes, it reveals the attitudes and purposes of its author
items.markingKey: C. Yes, it reveals the attitudes and purposes of its author. Bias is itself evidence

items.stem: An interpretation in history is
items.answer: a historian's explanation or judgement about the past
options: a historian's explanation or judgement about the past
items.markingKey: B. a historian's explanation or judgement about the past. Arguments built on evidence

items.stem: Why do historians writing in different periods often interpret the same event differently?
items.answer: They ask new questions and use new evidence shaped by their own times
options: They ask new questions and use new evidence shaped by their own times
items.markingKey: C. They ask new questions and use new evidence shaped by their own times. Context of the historian

items.stem: Historian A blames one leader for a war; Historian B blames long-term rivalries. Which approaches are these?
items.answer: Intentionalist (individual) versus structural
items.markingKey: C. Intentionalist (individual) versus structural. Agency versus structure

items.stem: Mussolini came to power in Italy in
items.markingKey: B. 1922. After the March on Rome

items.stem: Why did many Italians support Fascism after the First World War?
items.answer: Anger over the "mutilated victory", economic crisis and fear of communism
options: Anger over the "mutilated victory", economic crisis and fear of communism
items.markingKey: C. Anger over the "mutilated victory", economic crisis and fear of communism. Post-war grievances

items.stem: Why did Mussolini invade Abyssinia in 1935?
items.answer: To build an empire, gain prestige and avenge the defeat at Adwa
options: To help the League of Nations
To build an empire, gain prestige and avenge the defeat at Adwa
items.markingKey: C. To build an empire, gain prestige and avenge the defeat at Adwa. Imperial ambitions

items.stem: Stalin's rapid industrialisation programme was organised through
items.answer: Five-Year Plans
items.markingKey: A. Five-Year Plans. State targets

items.stem: The Great Terror of the 1930s involved
items.answer: show trials and mass purges of suspected opponents
options: the end of the secret police
show trials and mass purges of suspected opponents
items.markingKey: D. show trials and mass purges of suspected opponents. NKVD repression

items.stem: Why is collectivisation often judged a failure even though it supplied grain to cities?
items.answer: It caused famine and millions of deaths, and farm output fell
options: It caused famine and millions of deaths, and farm output fell
items.markingKey: D. It caused famine and millions of deaths, and farm output fell. Human cost and low productivity

items.stem: The Munich Agreement of 1938 allowed Germany to take
items.answer: the Sudetenland
items.subtopicHint: Appeasement and the road to war
items.markingKey: D. the Sudetenland. From Czechoslovakia

items.stem: Why did Britain follow a policy of appeasement?
items.answer: Fear of another war, military unreadiness and some sympathy for German grievances
items.subtopicHint: Appeasement and the road to war
options: Fear of another war, military unreadiness and some sympathy for German grievances
Britain wanted Germany to rule Europe
items.markingKey: A. Fear of another war, military unreadiness and some sympathy for German grievances. Several motives

items.stem: Why did the Nazi-Soviet Pact of 1939 make war more likely?
items.answer: It freed Hitler to invade Poland without fearing a war on two fronts
items.subtopicHint: Appeasement and the road to war
options: It freed Hitler to invade Poland without fearing a war on two fronts
It united Britain and the USSR
items.markingKey: B. It freed Hitler to invade Poland without fearing a war on two fronts. Removed a deterrent

items.stem: When comparing two sources, you should look for
items.answer: points of agreement and disagreement
items.markingKey: A. points of agreement and disagreement. Compare and contrast

items.stem: A cartoon from a British newspaper in 1938 mocks Hitler. What should you consider first about its purpose?
items.answer: Whether it aims to criticise appeasement or Hitler for a British audience
options: Whether it aims to criticise appeasement or Hitler for a British audience
How long it took to draw
items.markingKey: C. Whether it aims to criticise appeasement or Hitler for a British audience. Audience and message

items.stem: What does 'synthesis' mean in a source-based essay?
items.answer: Combining evidence from sources with your own knowledge into an argument
options: Combining evidence from sources with your own knowledge into an argument
items.markingKey: A. Combining evidence from sources with your own knowledge into an argument. Integration

items.stem: A state is usually defined by territory, population, government and
items.answer: sovereignty
items.markingKey: C. sovereignty. Four elements

items.stem: Human rights are
items.answer: rights everyone has simply because they are human
options: rights everyone has simply because they are human
items.markingKey: B. rights everyone has simply because they are human. Universal

items.stem: Why might people from different cultures prioritise different rights?
items.answer: Values such as community and individual freedom are weighted differently
options: Values such as community and individual freedom are weighted differently
items.markingKey: C. Values such as community and individual freedom are weighted differently. Universalism versus relativism

items.stem: Which piece of evidence is strongest?
items.answer: data from a large, representative survey
options: data from a large, representative survey
items.markingKey: D. data from a large, representative survey. Representative data

items.stem: 'Turnout fell after the new voting law, so the law caused it.' What is the flaw?
items.answer: It assumes correlation proves causation
items.markingKey: D. It assumes correlation proves causation. Other factors may explain it

items.stem: Why is a counter-argument useful in an essay?
items.answer: Answering it strengthens your conclusion
items.markingKey: B. Answering it strengthens your conclusion. Rebuttal

items.stem: Holding leaders answerable for their actions is
items.answer: accountability
items.markingKey: D. accountability. Answerability

items.stem: Which institution most directly checks the executive in a parliamentary democracy?
items.answer: the legislature
items.markingKey: D. the legislature. Questions, votes, committees

items.stem: Why can concentrated power be dangerous even under a popular leader?
items.answer: Without checks, it can be abused and is hard to remove
options: Without checks, it can be abused and is hard to remove
items.markingKey: A. Without checks, it can be abused and is hard to remove. Lord Acton

items.stem: A good research question should be
items.answer: focused enough to allow depth and debate
options: focused enough to allow depth and debate
answerable with yes or no only
items.markingKey: B. focused enough to allow depth and debate. Manageable scope

items.stem: Which is the best research question?
items.answer: To what extent has microfinance reduced poverty among women in Bangladesh since 2000?
options: To what extent has microfinance reduced poverty among women in Bangladesh since 2000?
items.markingKey: C. To what extent has microfinance reduced poverty among women in Bangladesh since 2000?. Specific, debatable, researchable

items.stem: Why should a research question permit different perspectives?
items.answer: So the report can weigh evidence and reach a supported judgement
options: So it can be answered in one line
So the report can weigh evidence and reach a supported judgement
items.markingKey: B. So the report can weigh evidence and reach a supported judgement. Debate is needed

items.stem: An interview you conduct yourself is
items.answer: primary research
items.markingKey: A. primary research. First-hand data

items.stem: Why might an online survey give a biased sample?
items.answer: Only people with internet access and interest will respond
options: Only people with internet access and interest will respond
items.markingKey: B. Only people with internet access and interest will respond. Self-selection

items.stem: Why combine qualitative interviews with quantitative surveys?
items.answer: Numbers show patterns while interviews explain reasons
options: Numbers show patterns while interviews explain reasons
items.markingKey: D. Numbers show patterns while interviews explain reasons. Mixed methods

items.stem: Reliability of a method means
items.answer: it would give similar results if repeated
options: it would give similar results if repeated
items.markingKey: A. it would give similar results if repeated. Consistency

items.stem: A study of 20 students claims to show the views of all teenagers. What is the main weakness?
items.answer: The sample is too small and not representative
options: The sample is too small and not representative
items.markingKey: B. The sample is too small and not representative. Generalisation

items.stem: Why should a researcher acknowledge the limitations of their own method?
items.answer: It shows critical awareness and lets readers judge the conclusions
options: It shows critical awareness and lets readers judge the conclusions
items.markingKey: D. It shows critical awareness and lets readers judge the conclusions. Reflective practice

items.stem: A bibliography lists
items.answer: the sources used in the report
options: the sources used in the report
items.markingKey: A. the sources used in the report. References

items.stem: Why must sources be referenced?
items.answer: To credit authors and let readers check the evidence
options: To credit authors and let readers check the evidence
items.markingKey: A. To credit authors and let readers check the evidence. Academic honesty

items.stem: A strong conclusion in a research report should
items.answer: answer the question with a judgement supported by the evidence
options: answer the question with a judgement supported by the evidence
repeat the introduction word for word
items.markingKey: C. answer the question with a judgement supported by the evidence. Supported answer

items.stem: Which gas contributes most to the enhanced greenhouse effect from human activity?
items.answer: carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: D. carbon dioxide. From burning fossil fuels

items.stem: The time between peak rainfall and peak discharge is the
items.answer: lag time
items.markingKey: C. lag time. On a hydrograph

items.stem: Why does urbanisation shorten lag time?
items.answer: Impermeable surfaces and drains send water to rivers faster
options: Impermeable surfaces and drains send water to rivers faster
items.markingKey: A. Impermeable surfaces and drains send water to rivers faster. Rapid runoff

items.stem: Natural increase is
items.answer: birth rate minus death rate
items.markingKey: B. birth rate minus death rate. Excludes migration

items.stem: In stage 3 of the DTM,
items.answer: birth rates fall while death rates are low
options: birth rates fall while death rates are low
items.markingKey: D. birth rates fall while death rates are low. Growth slows

items.stem: Why might an anti-natalist policy be introduced?
items.answer: To slow rapid population growth that strains resources
options: To slow rapid population growth that strains resources
items.markingKey: B. To slow rapid population growth that strains resources. Population control

items.stem: Which is a push factor?
items.answer: civil war
items.markingKey: D. civil war. Drives people away

items.stem: Internal migration means moving
items.answer: within the same country
items.markingKey: C. within the same country. Within borders

items.stem: Why can rural-urban migration create problems in the countryside?
items.answer: Young adults leave, leaving an ageing population and fewer workers
options: Young adults leave, leaving an ageing population and fewer workers
items.markingKey: A. Young adults leave, leaving an ageing population and fewer workers. Rural depopulation

items.stem: The ITCZ is a zone of
items.answer: low pressure where trade winds meet
options: low pressure where trade winds meet
items.markingKey: D. low pressure where trade winds meet. Intertropical Convergence Zone

items.stem: Humid tropical climates have
items.answer: high temperatures and rainfall all year
options: high temperatures and rainfall all year
items.markingKey: B. high temperatures and rainfall all year. Equatorial climate

items.stem: Why do savanna regions have a wet and a dry season?
items.answer: The ITCZ migrates north and south with the seasons
options: The ITCZ migrates north and south with the seasons
items.markingKey: D. The ITCZ migrates north and south with the seasons. Seasonal shift

items.stem: Chemical weathering is rapid in humid tropics because of
items.answer: high temperatures and abundant moisture
items.subtopicHint: Weathering and landforms in the tropics
items.markingKey: B. high temperatures and abundant moisture. Fast reactions

items.stem: A tor is
items.answer: an exposed outcrop of weathered granite
items.subtopicHint: Weathering and landforms in the tropics
options: an exposed outcrop of weathered granite
items.markingKey: D. an exposed outcrop of weathered granite. Granite landform

items.stem: Why can deep weathering profiles reach tens of metres in the tropics?
items.answer: Long periods of warm, wet conditions without glaciation
items.subtopicHint: Weathering and landforms in the tropics
options: Long periods of warm, wet conditions without glaciation
items.markingKey: A. Long periods of warm, wet conditions without glaciation. Time and climate

items.stem: The tallest trees that rise above the canopy are
items.answer: emergents
items.markingKey: B. emergents. Top layer

items.stem: Most nutrients in a tropical rainforest are stored in the
items.answer: biomass
items.markingKey: C. biomass. Rapid recycling

items.stem: Why do soils become infertile soon after rainforest is cleared?
items.answer: Heavy rain leaches nutrients once the biomass is removed
options: Heavy rain leaches nutrients once the biomass is removed
items.markingKey: A. Heavy rain leaches nutrients once the biomass is removed. Nutrient cycle broken

items.stem: Waves that build up beaches are
items.answer: constructive waves
items.markingKey: D. constructive waves. Strong swash

items.stem: Longshore drift moves sediment
items.answer: along the coast
items.markingKey: D. along the coast. Swash at an angle

items.stem: Why can building groynes on one beach increase erosion further along the coast?
items.answer: They trap sediment, starving beaches down-drift
options: They trap sediment, starving beaches down-drift
items.markingKey: B. They trap sediment, starving beaches down-drift. Sediment budget

items.stem: A bad harvest reduces the supply of wheat. What happens to price and quantity?
items.answer: Price rises, quantity falls
items.markingKey: B. Price rises, quantity falls. Supply shifts left

items.stem: A good with PED of -0.2 is
items.answer: price inelastic
items.markingKey: D. price inelastic. |PED| < 1

items.stem: A firm faces inelastic demand. What happens to total revenue if it raises price?
items.answer: It rises
items.markingKey: A. It rises. Quantity falls proportionately less

items.stem: Rent for a factory that does not change with output is a
items.answer: fixed cost
items.markingKey: B. fixed cost. Independent of output

items.stem: Total cost is 500 at 10 units and 560 at 11 units. What is the marginal cost of the 11th unit?
Why does marginal product eventually fall as more workers are added to a fixed machine?
items.answer: The law of diminishing returns
items.markingKey: A. The law of diminishing returns. Fixed factor constrains output

items.stem: In perfect competition, firms are
items.answer: price takers
items.markingKey: A. price takers. Many small firms, identical goods

items.stem: A market with only one seller is a
items.answer: monopoly
items.markingKey: B. monopoly. Single supplier

items.stem: Why can a monopoly charge a higher price than a competitive firm?
items.answer: It faces no close competitors, so buyers cannot switch easily
options: It faces no close competitors, so buyers cannot switch easily
It has higher costs by law
items.markingKey: A. It faces no close competitors, so buyers cannot switch easily. Market power

items.stem: GDP measures
items.answer: the value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year
options: the value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year
items.markingKey: A. the value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. Domestic output

items.stem: Why is real GDP better than nominal GDP for comparing output over time?
items.answer: It removes the effect of price changes
options: It removes the effect of price changes
items.markingKey: B. It removes the effect of price changes. Adjusted for inflation

items.stem: Nominal GDP grows 8% while prices rise 5%. Roughly what is real growth?
Inflation is
items.answer: a sustained rise in the general price level
options: a sustained rise in the general price level
items.markingKey: C. a sustained rise in the general price level. Measured by a price index

items.stem: Inflation caused by rising costs of production is
items.answer: cost-push inflation
items.markingKey: D. cost-push inflation. Higher input costs

items.stem: Why does unexpected inflation hurt savers with fixed interest?
items.answer: The real value of their savings falls
options: The real value of their savings falls
items.markingKey: A. The real value of their savings falls. Money buys less

items.stem: India's central bank is the
items.answer: Reserve Bank of India
items.markingKey: C. Reserve Bank of India. Bank of issue

items.stem: To reduce inflation, a central bank is likely to
items.answer: raise interest rates
items.markingKey: A. raise interest rates. Contractionary monetary policy

items.stem: How does a higher cash reserve ratio reduce lending?
items.answer: Banks must hold more deposits as reserves, leaving less to lend
options: It forces banks to lend more
Banks must hold more deposits as reserves, leaving less to lend
items.markingKey: D. Banks must hold more deposits as reserves, leaving less to lend. Lower credit creation

items.stem: A budget deficit occurs when
items.answer: government spending exceeds revenue
items.markingKey: A. government spending exceeds revenue. Government borrows

items.stem: Income tax is an example of a
items.answer: direct tax
items.markingKey: A. direct tax. Paid directly on income

items.stem: In a recession, why might a government increase spending?
items.answer: To boost aggregate demand and employment
options: To boost aggregate demand and employment
items.markingKey: D. To boost aggregate demand and employment. Expansionary fiscal policy

items.stem: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it

items.stem: Money doubles in 6 years at a fixed compound rate. In how many years does it become 8 times?
Boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 6 more boys join, the ratio is 1 : 1. How many students were there at first?
One pipe fills a tank in 6 hours; another empties it in 9 hours. If both are open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
items.answer: 18 hours

items.stem: Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'?
items.answer: found everywhere

items.stem: Author is to novel as composer is to ...
items.answer: symphony

items.stem: Some economists are writers. All writers are readers. Which statement must be true?
items.answer: Some economists are readers
items.explanation: The economists who are writers are also readers

items.stem: Claim: 'Since the new study app launched, the school's test scores rose, so the app raised scores.' Which fact, if true, most weakens the claim?
options: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
Students said they liked the app
items.answer: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
items.explanation: Another change at the same time offers a different explanation

items.stem: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, ?
items.answer: DW
items.explanation: First letters go forward, second letters go backward

items.stem: What comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?
Figures: shaded triangle, unshaded square, shaded pentagon, ... Each figure gains one side and the shading alternates. What is the next figure?
items.answer: an unshaded hexagon
items.explanation: Six sides, and the shading switches back to unshaded

items.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:15?
items.explanation: The hour hand has moved a quarter of 30° past the 3

items.stem: From home you walk 4 km north and then 3 km east. How far are you from home in a straight line?
items.answer: 5 km

items.stem: A 3 x 3 x 3 cube is painted on all faces and cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly one painted face?
items.explanation: One at the centre of each face
